newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Spain and Morocco plan to set up free trade zone.
newsitem.headline: Spain and Morocco plan to set up free trade zone.

text.p: Morocco and Spain have signed an initial accord for plans to build a 40 hectares (100 acres) free trade zone in the north Moroccan city of Nador, the Moroccan news agency MAP said on Wednesday
It said the project would accommodate about 150 medium-sized businesses and generate up to 10,000 jobs. It is part of plans to promote the economy of the northern provinces.

The accord was signed on Tuesday by Trade, Industry and Handicrafts Minister Driss Jettou and Spain's Lorenzo Victor Salamanca, President of L.V. Salamanca Holding, which deals with industrial management.

The European Union is helping Morocco in its efforts to transform the economy of the northern provinces, where many people are involved in the cultivation of cannabis and which is also a springboard for many illegal immigrants trying to get to Europe.
Morocco early last year launched a big crackdown on drug traffickers, many of whom leave from northern Morocco for Spain and other parts of Europe.
Around 20 percent of Morocco's estimated 27 million people live in the northern area.
